<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
<!-- PR 2 — branch: gdn-prefill-state-pool (12614958b8), base: upstream/main (5cf5c8fa6d). -->

## Overview

Let FlashInfer GDN prefill read and write SSM states in the cache pool in place (Qwen3.5/3.8, Qwen3-Next linear attention), removing 4-5 gather/mask/cast/scatter kernels per layer when all prefill rows are fresh or all have cached context. Mixed batches keep the gather path. Includes fixes for two engine-killing crashes found in validation/review: bf16-pool checkpointing and strided state indices with MTP configured. Related: #64419 (FlashInfer prefill output in place).

## Claims

- **Removes the per-layer state gather/mask/cast/scatter kernels entirely** on none/all batches — measured −249 µs of `index_elementwise` plus −118 µs of fill/cast kernels per chunked prefill (18 GDN layers, profile diff below).
- **Forward time −2.7% (8k prefill), −7.6% (chunked prefill), −4.9% (mixed batch)** vs current main; decode unchanged.
- **Side effect: FlashInfer's checkpoint-emitting kernel loses most of its premium** — with `initial_state=None` it runs 358 → 275 µs/layer at 8k (align-mode checkpointed prefill, 48 GDN layers: 17.3 → 13.2 ms per prefill).
- **Fixes an engine-killing crash on Qwen3-Next** (bf16 `mamba_ssm_dtype`): the first checkpointed multi-row batch hits a FlashInfer compile error (`autovec_copy ... BFloat16 and Float32`); checkpointed prefills over a non-fp32 pool now gather into fp32 as before.
- **Fixes the first pool-route prefill crashing with MTP configured**: FlashInfer rejects strided state indices; both metadata-builder paths now materialize contiguous indices.
- **GSM8K unchanged** (A/B below); route-level parity pinned harder: pool ≡ gather (1e-3) and pool ≡ CuteDSL backend as an independent whole-layer reference.
- 5 files, +489/−16 (mostly tests). No new kernels, no new host syncs.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

`vllm bench forward` (graph-replayed, sample spread ≤0.6%), Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (18 GDN layers), one B300, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. Base is current main (5cf5c8fa6d), PR is this branch rebased onto it:

| case (forward) | main (µs) | PR (µs) | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 8192 | 12481.6 | 12139.5 | −2.7% |
| chunked prefill 2048@10240 | 4682.8 | 4327.5 | −7.6% |
| mix (64 decode + 4096 prefill) | 8894.5 | 8458.2 | −4.9% |
| decode 256×1@8192 | 6785.0 | 6786.9 | ~0 |

Kernel diff (chunked prefill, main → PR): `index_elementwise` 36→0 launches (−249 µs, state gather + scatter), fill/cast elementwise 54→0 (−118 µs, mask + fp32 casts). No compensating regressions.

<details>
<summary>In-process single-request prefill bench (Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, GB300)</summary>

In-process `LLM`, one fresh random prompt per request, `max_tokens=1`, median of 24 requests (2 fresh processes per arm, forward+reverse order). "GPU" = device time of one profiled prefill; "hit" = the same prompt repeated (prefix-cache hit). Base arm is main immediately after #64419 merged (its content); the wrapper-contract cleanup in the merge does not affect prefill kernels.

| arm | 512 wall / GPU (ms) | 1024 | 2048 | 8192 | 8192 hit (wall) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 25.5 / 14.7 | 36.3 / 23.4 | 168.8 / 38.4 | 155.7 / 144.9 | 33.3 |
| PR | 18.7 / 13.4 | 27.8 / 21.6 | 166.6 / 36.1 | 149.2 / 139.8 | 23.8 |

Per layer at 8k: FlashInfer chunk (checkpointing, align mode) 357.8 → 275.1 µs; state gather + mask + cast + scatter ~50 µs → gone. Eager prefills above 1024 tokens are host bound (~170 ms wall for 40-148 ms of GPU work), so 2k-8k wall moves less than GPU time.

Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-NVFP4 (bf16 states; checkpointed prefills keep the gather route, see Details): wall −30% at 512-1k and on prefix-cache hits, neutral at 2k-8k; GPU −2.3% at 2k-8k, −9..−11% at 512-1k.
</details>

### E2E performance

`vllm serve Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 16384` (default compile), random dataset, seed 0, one B300 node, main and PR servers on identical configs, main arm first:

| metric | main | PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT 8k-in/1-out c1 (ms, 30 prompts) | 140.82 | 137.96 | −2.0% |
| TTFT 2k-in/1-out c1 (ms, 60 prompts) | 144.16 | 133.78 | −7.2% |
| TPOT 1k/512 c1 (ms) | 4.35 | 4.34 | ~0 |
| TPOT 1k/512 c16 (ms) | 6.78 | 6.83 | +0.7% (noise) |
| TPOT 8k/1024 c64 (ms, medians across 4 rounds) | 12.94–13.61 | 12.98–14.00 | noise |
| TTFT 8k/1024 c64 (ms, medians across 4 rounds) | 1745–3932 | 1825–9669 | see note |

TTFT at c1 sits on a ~140 ms host-bound floor, so the 8k row moves little while 2k (GPU-heavier fraction) moves more; TPOT is decode-side and unchanged by this PR, as designed. The c64 config is high-variance with a fresh server per arm: mean TTFT differs up to 2-3× between identical-code runs in alternating rounds (a run-order artifact — the second server of each pair is slower regardless of which code it runs; root cause not pinned), while per-round medians are within noise of each other. A profiled pair with the warmup fully settled shows parity: main 16.62s vs PR 16.97s total duration (+2%), equal TPOT. The forward microbenchmark above is the controlled measurement for the prefill change.

Across 8 A/B server logs (4 rounds × main/PR), every CuTe-DSL compile completed before `Application startup complete`; none compiled during serving. In-serving JIT monitor warnings were pre-existing Triton kernels identical on both arms: `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel`, `_fused_post_conv_kernel` at TP2, and the model's sparse-attention kernels.

### Accuracy

GSM8K five-shot chat completions, temp 0, full test set (1319 questions), same server setup as e2e:

| arm | flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9242 / 0.9196 |
| PR | 0.9196 / 0.9158 |

Difference within run noise (±0.0075 stderr, and batching-dependent at temp 0).

Route-level correctness (stronger than e2e sampling noise): the new suite runs the real `_forward_core` on metadata from the real `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` and asserts pool ≡ gather (1e-3) and pool ≡ the CuteDSL backend as an independent whole-layer reference, including exported checkpoints, over fp32 and bf16 pools.

### Tests

- New `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_flashinfer.py`: 8 batch shapes × 2 dtypes (fp32/bf16), 2 spec-configured cases, and 16 checkpointed cases (fp32/bf16 pools × `use_cp` auto/False). NaN-poisoned output buffers expose unwritten rows; checks pool/gather/CuteDSL parity. With the bf16 fallback disabled, the 4 bf16 + `use_cp=False` cases fail with the FlashInfer compile error.
- `test_pool_route_with_spec_decode_configured` (fp32/bf16) runs the real builder + `_forward_core` pool route with `num_spec=1`, asserting contiguous indices and parity vs CuteDSL; fails before the fix. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 was also checked directly: both regular and CP routes reject strided indices.
- Metadata-builder test pins host-side mode vs device-side `prefill_has_initial_state` agreement, spec rows included.
- **135 passed on B300 at head `12614958b8`**: `tests/kernels/mamba/{test_gdn_forward_core_flashinfer.py,test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py,test_gdn_forward_core_split.py,test_gdn_fused_mtp.py}` and `tests/v1/attention/{test_gdn_metadata_builder.py,test_gdn_zero_draft_spec_rows.py}`. During development on GB300: 130 passed, 2 skipped for PR test files + warmup test; 391 passed, 2 skipped for related GDN/mamba files. Route tests fail on each injected bug (pool route reading no initial state, wrong in-place slice, decode rows not stored).
- CI: adds `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_flashinfer.py`, the `gdn_attn.py` / mamba GDN source dependencies, and `tests/v1/attention/utils.py` to the `:nvidia: (B200) Kernels` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. That step names test files explicitly and previously listed only `test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py` for GDN prefill; the H200-MIG mamba step collects the directory but this module skips on SM90.
- `tests/models/.../test_gdn_sleep_wake.py`, `test_hybrid.py -k qwen3-next` fail on base and PR alike (unrelated: unquantized FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE weight conversion).

## Details

- **Host-side mode**: computed from `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`, exact for prefill rows, so it agrees with the device-side `prefill_has_initial_state` mask; the `_prefill_initial_state_mode` docstring states the invariant and the builder test pins it, spec rows included. Any shape ambiguity falls back to "mixed" = today's gather path, and "mixed" is the default for builders that don't compute it.
- **In-place states**: mode "none" → `initial_state=None` (zero start), final states written to pool rows via `output_state`/`state_indices`; mode "all" → the pool is also the initial-state source. Per prefill row this avoids moving `num_v_heads × head_v_dim × head_k_dim` fp32 twice per layer, and pool states stay in the cache dtype (never cast as a whole pool).
- **bf16-pool fallback (crash fix)**: FlashInfer 0.7.2's regular (non-CP) checkpointing kernel does not compile when it reads/writes a bf16 pool in place while storing fp32 checkpoints; the CP kernel is unaffected but serving batches take the regular one. Checkpointed prefills over a non-fp32 pool force "mixed" (gather into fp32, as before) and warmup skips the uncompilable variants, so graph capture can't hit them either. Found on Qwen3-Next, where the first checkpointed multi-row batch killed the engine.
- **MTP-configured prefill (crash fix)**: mamba block-table rows have `1 + num_spec` state slots. A prefill-only batch takes the non-spec branch, yielding a strided column-0 view as `prefill_state_indices`. FlashInfer's regular route raises `ValueError: Mismatched s_indices.strides[0] ... expected to be 1`; CP raises `RuntimeError: state_indices must be contiguous`. Both `build()` and `update_block_table()` now use `torch.Tensor.contiguous()` (a no-op without spec decode), preventing the first pool-route prefill from killing the engine.

Dispatch cases (all tested):

| case | route |
|---|---|
| fresh rows | pool, `initial_state=None` |
| all-cached rows | pool as initial and final state |
| mixed fresh/cached rows | gather + mask + scatter |
| non-spec decodes + prefills | peeled decodes to `[:num_decodes]`, prefill in place |
| align-mode checkpoints, fp32 pool | checkpointing call with pool route |
| align-mode checkpoints, bf16 pool | gather |
| spec decodes + prefills | pool route, FlashInfer-allocated output, `index_copy_` merge |
| prefill-only, MTP configured | pool route with contiguous state indices |

- Limitations: mixed batches see no state-traffic win. Measured on GB300/B300 (SM103); SM90/SM120 not run (FlashInfer documents the APIs there). TP2 smoke passed (server up, 8k/64 c8 32/32 OK, GSM8K 0.8567); one known pre-existing warmup-coverage gap (`_fused_post_conv_kernel` JIT warning at TP2 only — applies to base too).
- Overlap audit (2026-10-29): #50372 (open) fuses the FlashInfer prefill state I/O with Triton gather/scatter kernels — this PR removes that I/O for none/all batches instead; its fused kernels would still apply to mixed batches and bf16 checkpointed prefills, so the two compose. #41824 (open) is the Triton-backend counterpart (in-place SSM state for the Triton chunk kernel). #60659 (checkpoints for Triton/FLA + FlyDSL) and #55876 (grouped prefill) touch the same files, textual overlap only. #64303 changes which slots prefills read/write; `state_indices` passes that through unchanged. #64419 (merged) is the output-buffer counterpart (FlashInfer prefill output in place).

AI assistance was used in the creation of this PR; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the validations above.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The FlashInfer prefill routes of ``QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward_core``.
+
+Each batch runs through the real ``_forward_core`` on metadata from the real
+``GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder``, along every route it can take:
+
+* state pool (``prefill_initial_state_mode`` "none"/"all"): FlashInfer reads
+  and writes the SSM cache slots in place;
+* gather (forced "mixed"): the caller gathers, masks and scatters states;
+* the CuteDSL chunk kernel, an independent reference for the whole layer
+  (conv, output placement behind peeled decodes, state writes);
+* with internal prefill checkpoints (align mode), pool vs gather.
+
+``core_attn_out`` is allocated uninitialized; it is NaN-poisoned here so any
+actual row the layer fails to write shows up.
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+import functools
+import types
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not (
+    current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+):
+    pytest.skip(
+        reason="Compares the FlashInfer and CuteDSL GDN prefill (CUDA SM10x).",
+        allow_module_level=True,
+    )
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig, set_current_vllm_config  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.checkpoint import (  # noqa: E402
+    MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter,
+    MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn import qwen_gdn_linear_attn  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn.qwen_gdn_linear_attn import (  # noqa: E402
+    ChunkGatedDeltaRule,
+    QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    MambaStateShapeCalculator,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import (  # noqa: E402
+    GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder,
+    GDNFlashInferCheckpointPlan,
+    plan_flashinfer_checkpoints,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import NULL_BLOCK_ID  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec  # noqa: E402
+
+H, HV, K, V = 4, 8, 128, 128
+CONV_KERNEL = 4
+CONV_DIM = 2 * H * K + HV * V
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+PREFIX = "model.layers.0.linear_attn"
+PAD = 16  # CUDA graph padding rows behind num_actual_tokens
+
+
+def _builder(backend: str, num_spec: int = 0):
+    cfg = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        hf_config_override={"linear_key_head_dim": K},
+    )
+    cfg.additional_config = {"gdn_prefill_backend": backend}
+    if num_spec:
+        cfg.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=num_spec
+        )
+    builder = GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder(
+        kv_cache_spec=MambaSpec(
+            block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+            shapes=((16, 64),),
+            dtypes=(torch.float16,),
+            num_speculative_blocks=num_spec,
+        ),
+        layer_names=[PREFIX],
+        vllm_config=cfg,
+        device=torch.device("cuda"),
+    )
+    assert builder.gdn_prefill_backend == backend
+    return cfg, builder
+
+
+def _layer(cfg, weights, conv_state, ssm_state, packed_decode=False):
+    layer = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        prefix=PREFIX,
+        enable_packed_recurrent_decode=packed_decode,
+        tp_size=1,
+        num_k_heads=H,
+        num_v_heads=HV,
+        head_k_dim=K,
+        head_v_dim=V,
+        key_dim=H * K,
+        value_dim=HV * V,
+        activation="silu",
+        A_log=weights["A_log"],
+        dt_bias=weights["dt_bias"],
+        conv1d=types.SimpleNamespace(
+            weight=weights["conv_weight"], bias=weights["conv_bias"]
+        ),
+        kv_cache=(conv_state, ssm_state),
+        _checkpoint_buffer_spec=((64, HV, V, K), torch.float32),
+        _checkpoint_exporter=MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter(state_len=CONV_KERNEL - 1),
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(cfg):
+        layer.chunk_gated_delta_rule = ChunkGatedDeltaRule()
+    layer.gdn_prefill_backend = layer.chunk_gated_delta_rule.gdn_prefill_backend
+    for name in (
+        "rearrange_mixed_qkv",
+        "_forward_core",
+        "_forward_core_decode_non_spec",
+        "_forward_flashinfer_prefill",
+    ):
+        method = getattr(QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention, name)
+        setattr(layer, name, types.MethodType(method, layer))
+    return layer
+
+
+def _run(cfg, meta, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0, packed_decode=False):
+    """Returns (core_attn_out with padding rows, conv_state, ssm_state)."""
+    conv_state, ssm_state = conv_state0.clone(), ssm_state0.clone()
+    layer = _layer(cfg, weights, conv_state, ssm_state, packed_decode)
+    mixed_qkv, b, a = inputs
+    num_tokens = mixed_qkv.shape[0] + PAD
+    # Uninitialized in serving; NaN here so any row left unwritten shows.
+    core_attn_out = torch.full(
+        (num_tokens, HV, V), float("nan"), dtype=mixed_qkv.dtype, device="cuda"
+    )
+
+    def pad(x):
+        return torch.cat([x, torch.zeros_like(x[:PAD])])
+
+    ctx = types.SimpleNamespace(attn_metadata={PREFIX: meta})
+    with patch.object(qwen_gdn_linear_attn, "get_forward_context", return_value=ctx):
+        layer._forward_core(
+            mixed_qkv=pad(mixed_qkv), b=pad(b), a=pad(a), core_attn_out=core_attn_out
+        )
+    return core_attn_out, conv_state, ssm_state
+
+
+def _setup(seq_lens, query_lens, state_dtype, gen):
+    batch = BatchSpec(seq_lens=seq_lens, query_lens=query_lens)
+    common = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch, BLOCK_SIZE, torch.device("cuda"), arange_block_indices=True
+    )
+    pool_size = int(common.block_table_tensor.max().item()) + 2
+    conv_shape, ssm_shape = MambaStateShapeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_shape(
+        1, H, HV, K, V, CONV_KERNEL, num_spec=0
+    )
+
+    def randn(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, scale=0.1):
+        return (
+            torch.randn(*shape, generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+            * scale
+        ).to(dtype)
+
+    conv_state0 = randn(pool_size, *conv_shape, scale=0.05)
+    ssm_state0 = randn(pool_size, *ssm_shape, dtype=state_dtype, scale=0.05)
+    weights = dict(
+        A_log=randn(HV, dtype=torch.float32),
+        dt_bias=randn(HV, dtype=torch.float32),
+        conv_weight=randn(CONV_DIM, 1, CONV_KERNEL),
+        conv_bias=randn(CONV_DIM),
+    )
+    num_tokens = sum(query_lens)
+    inputs = (randn(num_tokens, CONV_DIM), randn(num_tokens, HV), randn(num_tokens, HV))
+    return common, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0
+
+
+# (decode seq lens, prefill seq lens, prefill query lens, expected mode)
+CASES = {
+    "one_fresh": ([], [300], [300], "none"),
+    "one_cached": ([], [337], [300], "all"),
+    "fresh_rows": ([], [200, 64, 5], [200, 64, 5], "none"),
+    "cached_rows": ([], [237, 101, 42], [200, 64, 5], "all"),
+    "mixed_rows": ([], [237, 64, 42], [200, 64, 5], "mixed"),
+    "decodes_fresh": ([64, 64, 64], [300, 64], [300, 64], "none"),
+    "decodes_cached": ([64, 64, 64], [337], [300], "all"),
+    # Packed decode (its own early-return path) vs the peeled-decode kernel.
+    "decodes_only": ([64, 64, 64], [], [], "mixed"),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("state_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES.values(), ids=CASES.keys())
+def test_flashinfer_prefill_routes_match(case, state_dtype):
+    decode_seq_lens, prefill_seq_lens, prefill_query_lens, mode = case
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    seq_lens = decode_seq_lens + prefill_seq_lens
+    query_lens = [1] * len(decode_seq_lens) + prefill_query_lens
+    common, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0 = _setup(
+        seq_lens, query_lens, state_dtype, gen
+    )
+    num_actual = sum(query_lens)
+
+    fi_cfg, fi_builder = _builder("flashinfer")
+    with set_current_vllm_config(fi_cfg):
+        meta = fi_builder.build(common_prefix_len=0, common_attn_metadata=common)
+    assert meta.prefill_initial_state_mode == mode
+    meta_gather = dataclasses.replace(meta, prefill_initial_state_mode="mixed")
+    ref_cfg, ref_builder = _builder("cutedsl")
+    with set_current_vllm_config(ref_cfg):
+        meta_ref = ref_builder.build(common_prefix_len=0, common_attn_metadata=common)
+
+    packed = not prefill_seq_lens
+    runs = {
+        "pool": _run(fi_cfg, meta, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0, packed),
+        "gather": _run(fi_cfg, meta_gather, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0),
+        "cutedsl": _run(ref_cfg, meta_ref, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0),
+    }
+    for out, _, _ in runs.values():
+        assert not out[:num_actual].isnan().any(), "unwritten output rows"
+
+    out, conv_state, ssm_state = runs["pool"]
+    # The pool route changes only where FlashInfer reads/writes states.
+    # Outputs are compared over the actual rows only: padding rows behind
+    # num_actual_tokens are uninitialized by contract.
+    gather_out, gather_conv, gather_ssm = runs["gather"]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out[:num_actual], gather_out[:num_actual], atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv_state, gather_conv, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ssm_state, gather_ssm, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+    # Different chunk kernels: tolerances of the kernel-level parity tests.
+    tol = 2e-2 if state_dtype == torch.float32 else 6e-2
+    ref_out, ref_conv, ref_ssm = runs["cutedsl"]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out[:num_actual], ref_out[:num_actual], atol=tol, rtol=tol
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv_state, ref_conv, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ssm_state, ref_ssm, atol=tol, rtol=tol)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("state_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_pool_route_with_spec_decode_configured(state_dtype):
+    """With spec decode configured, block table rows hold 1 + num_spec state
+    slots, so a prefill-only batch (no drafted rows, non-spec branch) gets a
+    strided column-0 view as its state indices; the pool route must make them
+    contiguous before FlashInfer's kernels (which reject strided indices)."""

+    seq_lens = query_lens = [200, 64, 5]

+        seq_lens, query_lens, state_dtype, gen
+    )
+    num_actual = sum(query_lens)
+    fi_cfg, fi_builder = _builder("flashinfer", num_spec=1)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(fi_cfg):
+        meta = fi_builder.build(common_prefix_len=0, common_attn_metadata=common)

+    out, conv, ssm = _run(fi_cfg, meta, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0)

+        ref_cfg, meta_ref, weights, inputs, conv_state0, ssm_state0
+    )
+    tol = 2e-2 if state_dtype == torch.float32 else 6e-2
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out[:num_actual], ref_out[:num_actual], atol=tol, rtol=tol
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv, ref_conv, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ssm, ref_ssm, atol=tol, rtol=tol)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cp", ["auto", False])
